note: The complement of sequential/v2vhdl_blocking_readback: where that one needs a VHDL variable to reproduce Verilog's immediate assignment, this one needs plain signal assignments and nothing more. Both statements are non-blocking, so q receives p's previous contents and the pair is a two-stage shift register; a lowering that makes either assignment immediate collapses it to one stage and q equals p. VHDL signal semantics already match, so this is the case that must be left alone rather than translated - which is its own way to get wrong. d is one-hot and advances every step so the one-edge lag shows on every row.
